key_insight: Different flow paths can yield the same flow-matching objective yet produce very different SGD variance and convergence speed.
engineering_relevance: For training generative models, path design is an optimization knob that can materially reduce training cost without changing the underlying target distribution.
method: Analyze SGD variance under the family of paths with identical marginals and velocity field.
Derive tight iteration-complexity bounds for a linear model in 1D Gaussian settings and identify an optimal linear path.
Formulate PathOpt_θ to choose variance-minimizing paths under verifiable sample-based constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theory plus experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets to validate the variance-reduction effect.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the same-marginal constraint G(p_t, v_t^*); ignoring it can actually slow convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
